text: Just then the generals cook, Prokhor. <break time="0.8s" /> Came by and Ochumelov called him over to ask about the dog. <break time="0.8s" /> Is this your dog, Prokhor, he asked. <break time="0.8s" /> And the cook answered. <break time="0.8s" /> What an idea. <break time="0.8s" /> We have never had a dog like that. <break time="0.8s" /> Then there is no need to ask any more. <break time="0.8s" /> For it is just a stray dog. <break time="0.8s" /> And it must be destroyed. <break time="0.8s" /> It is not ours. <break time="0.8s" /> Prokhor went on but it belongs to the generals brother. <break time="0.8s" /> Who arrived here the other day. <break time="0.8s" /> And likes borzois. <break time="0.8s" /> At these words. <break time="0.8s" /> Ochumelovs whole face filled. <break time="0.8s" /> With a warm, tender smile. <break time="0.8s" /> Vladimir Ivanich has come. <break time="0.8s" /> I did not even know it. <break time="0.8s" /> So it is his dog. <break time="0.8s" /> Then take it, by all means. <break time="0.8s" /> It is a fine, lively little pup. <break time="0.8s" /> And it snapped at this fellows finger. <break time="0.8s" /> Ha ha ha. <break time="0.8s" /> Come now, why are you shaking. <break time="0.8s" /> You little rascal. <break time="0.8s" /> Prokhor called the dog. <break time="0.8s" /> And walked away from the woodyard with it. <break time="0.8s" /> While the whole crowd laughed at Khryukin. <break time="0.8s" /> I will deal with you later. <break time="0.8s" /> Ochumelov warned Khryukin. <break time="0.8s" /> And wrapping himself in his coat. <break time="0.8s" /> He went on his way. <break time="0.8s" /> Across the market square.
